pull_requests.title: Resolve spatial common-tangent nullness (OWR Conjecture 4); published preprint
pull_requests.body:
This result resolves Conjecture 4 in OWR 44/2008 for three pairwise disjoint convex subsets of R³: the spatial union of their complete common tangent lines has Lebesgue outer measure zero. The stronger Conjecture 3 is outside this result's scope.

The accepted research note is **The spatial locus of common tangents to three disjoint convex sets is null**, by Alec Kriebel, published with its verification package at [DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23127955](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23127955). ## Result

A compact connected two-dimensional counterexample to Krener's printed manifold conjecture: completeness and negative curvature of the actual finite-time observation Gramian do not force global observability.

Take a connected two-sheet cover of a closed genus-two hyperbolic surface, a smooth Nash isometric embedding of the base into R17, observation through the cover, and zero dynamics. The state surface has genus three. For every fixed T>0 the exact Gramian is P_T=Tπ*g, complete with sectional curvature −1/T. It is uniformly positive and bounded relative to a fixed smooth background metric, with explicit bounds in a fixed finite atlas. The observation is locally injective, yet every attained output history has exactly two distinct initial states.

The original local-coordinate manifold formulation does not require simple connectivity, a global Euclidean state domain, nonzero dynamics, or a restricted output dimension. This result addresses that formulation; no strengthened Euclidean or simply connected claim is made.

This is an application of classical hyperbolic geometry, covering theory, and Nash's smooth compact embedding theorem (1956, Theorem 2, p. 59). Hermann–Krener1977 Example 3.3 already demonstrates local/global observation ambiguity. Its one-dimensional example has no sectional two-planes, preventing an unqualified first-refutation claim across every literal dimensional reading. The present theorem has dimension two and genuine curvature −1/T.

pull_requests.body:
## Complete sufficient-condition candidate

For every real alpha, define a=|1−alpha|, b=|alpha| and k=(a+2b−1+sqrt((a+2b−1)^2+8b))/4. The condition

Σ n[1+k(n−1)] |a_n| ≤ 1

implies membership in Miller's alpha-convex class. It guarantees zero avoidance and strict positivity inside the unit disk, including the equality budget. At alpha=0 and 1 it recovers the source's n and n² coefficient weights exactly.

For 0<alpha≤1, the interpolation parameter is sharp within this specific one-parameter weight family. No optimality for other weights or outside that range is claimed. This is not the stronger fixed-C log-squared statement announced at smaller c in the source, and the exhaustive scan is not claimed polynomial-time.

pull_requests.body:
## Counterexample to the literal unaveraged birational-map limit

The fixed map **L(u,v)=(u,(u²+1)v)** is birational over Q, with rational inverse (u,v/(u²+1)). For every prime **p≡3 mod4**, both directions are defined everywhere on F_p² and are inverse permutations. Every point lies on a cycle.

For the original point-weighted statistic D_p(x)=p⁻² #{z:T_p(z)≤px}, the unchanged proof gives, for **every fixed 1/2≤x<1**, limsup D_p(x)=1 and liminf D_p(x)≤23/24 along that same positive-density prime class. In particular there is no limit at x=3/4, nor any weak limiting cycle-length distribution. This is failure on an interval, not only at a possible limiting atom.

The argument combines exact fiber cycle counts, elementary character/Jacobi identities and the **unconditional** prime-average totient theorem plus Dirichlet/progression results. It does not assume GRH or Artin's fixed-base primitive-root conjecture. An arithmetic mean is a proof tool for extracting one subsequence, not a substitute for the source's unaveraged limit.

### Source boundary

Vivaldi's OWR54/2004 Conjecture1, pp.2944–2945, permits birational maps and suitable positive-density reduction primes. The example has a polynomial forward map and a rational inverse; it is **not** a polynomial automorphism over C. ## Credited resolution of the literal 2007 étale question

Status: **already_solved, 1/5 substantive author turns**, as a source-version clarification. The classical Russell-form family y^p = x + t x^p over the t-line has smooth geometrically integral affine-line fibers in characteristic p, but no dominant étale base change can trivialize it. A finite purely inseparable degree-p base change does trivialize it. Russell’s 1970 paper explicitly gives the same generic form; no novelty claim is made.

**The later finite-degree question and the Q-bar case remain untouched.** OWR2007 p.69 asks for an étale conclusion over all algebraically closed fields and names F_p-bar or Q-bar. The packet compares the exact primary versions and corrects the lost overbars in the import.

The total space is integral; the relative derivative is -1, so the family is smooth, flat and dominant. Explicit substitutions identify each geometric fiber with A¹. A generic extension supplied by a dominant étale map is finite separable; a polynomial affine-line parametrization would force t to be a p-th power by leading coefficients, contradicting separability. This is not a nonreduced-fiber example or a search over finitely many covers.

## Result and classical credit

Rank 686, ID **2306078 / AMR-022-6078**, Hayman–Lingham Problem 6.78: **already_solved**, after **3/5 substantive approaches**.

For every holomorphic injective map on the open unit disk with `f(0)=0` and complex derivative `f'(0)=1`, the minimum spherical area of its image is **one half of the sphere**, uniquely attained by **`f(z)=z`**. This equals **`2*pi`** for unit-sphere density `4/(1+|w|^2)^2`, or **`pi/2`** in the quarter-area convention. No convexity, coefficient-reality, boundedness, degree, or boundary-extension assumption is added.

pull_requests.body:
## Disposition

**Original AIM target: unsolved, 3/5 approaches.** The independent audit passes the explicitly scoped regular-local theorem and singular F-pure counterexample. The original primary AIM ring conventions remain unverified (the problem page returned 502/timeouts). No novelty, first-resolution, or human-peer-review claim is made.

## Qualified mathematical result

For an F-finite Noetherian regular local ring of characteristic `p>0`, and nonzero proper ideals `I_n` for every positive `n` with `I_a I_b ⊆ I_(a+b)`, the limit `lim_n n fpt_R(I_n)` exists and equals `sup_n n fpt_R(I_n)` **in the extended positive reals, allowing positive infinity**. Descendingness and finite generation of the Rees algebra are unnecessary.

The separate singular example uses `R=(F_p[x,y,z]/(xy))_(x,y,z)`, `I_(2a)=(z^a)`, and `I_(2a+1)=((x+y)z^(a+1))`. Its two-generated Rees algebra has nonzero proper terms containing nonzerodivisors, while normalized thresholds alternate between 2 and 0. It refutes an unrestricted F-pure-ring reading; it does not settle a target implicitly requiring regularity or strong F-regularity.

The acceptance note qualifies Koley–Kumar attribution: the named invariant concerns descending filtrations with finite limit; infinity uses their common extended upper/lower limits, and arbitrary graded crossing is an extension. Global, non-F-finite, singular strongly F-regular, and zero-term variants are not claimed resolved.

pull_requests.body:
## Credited prior resolution, with independent audit PASS

Problem **30005519** (rank **799**, **OWR-13750332-001**).

The complete cleaned target has an affirmative answer: for every n >= 1 and even r >= 2, the maximum real vector-space dimension of an e_r-zero subspace of R^n is **min(n,r-1)**. pull_requests.body:
## Conditional verification, with the original scope hold retained

Record 30003846, Oberwolfach Questions 71–72. This draft publishes an audit of prior work credited to Gili Golan, [arXiv:2607.10961v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10961v1), submitted 12 July 2026. No new result, novelty claim, journal acceptance, or fresh proof-search attempt is asserted.

The connected-crossing-graph classification passes with the stated representation/core and finiteness imports. The first audit left its unproved I0 bridge open. The later decomposition supplement has now passed independent review and closes that mathematical gap under the explicit restricted permutational convention: finite-support base, potentially nonfaithful indexing action, and the full acting group retained as top factor.

The original question passage does not define the wreath indexing action. Narrower regular-only and faithful-action-only exclusions remain uncertified, so this is conditional prior-proof verification with a terminology/scope hold. Question 109 is not certified. The explicit finite-support/nonfaithful convention is attributed to Bleak–Brin–Moore §3.5 and the supplement; Golan's introduction states permutational without separately spelling out those details.

Start with [ACCEPTANCE.md](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/audit/fast-bump-30003846-conditional-scope/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30003846/ACCEPTANCE.md). It explains the chronology, current verdict, limitations and retained attribution. The connected reconstruction, historical audit, supplement, independent review and contextual correction patches are included.

## Exact queue and publication scope

Only the unique 30003846 row's Findings cell changes in unsolved_math_prioritization/QUEUE.md. Status stays queued, Turns stays 0/5. Every other cell, row, note, existing chat link and literal digest is byte-preserved. No already_solved or exhausted designation is made.

Base commit: 6ca1e663ab556636a3c2a9b67a96274ef95e8bab
Before-QUEUE: 397331 bytes; SHA-256 25fdcea7fdcb23109e4b46ba2b560dcff02c18aeed35899c4d89375e3de6cdfe
After-QUEUE: 397785 bytes; SHA-256 fac278d72caa7fcfe95c64ddde331c25c1427bb91559b91e52ff30858629bb4a

The new packet contains authored mathematical analysis/code and public verification metadata only. It excludes source-document bodies, dataset contents, private sources and private coordination. The separately authorized existing full queue is preserved except for the stated Findings change. The source metadata distinguishes historical retrieval/inspection from the fresh local rehash performed for this delivery.

## Reproducibility

The original programs had 41 assertion guards that disappeared under -O/-OO, and original read-only executions failed on their sidecar writes. The separately identified hardened derivatives use explicit conditional raises and stdout-only output. Their original/derivative hashes, contextual patch and fresh local exact-AST transformation receipt are included; standalone original programs and superseded full-packet verifiers are not shipped.

All three finite suites are freshly replayed normally, with -O, and with -OO under UID/EUID 1000 on a 0555/0444 packet and actual before/after QUEUE files. Physical create/append-open attempts are denied and inputs remain unchanged. Complete raw stdout/stderr are retained and compared to full pinned references. Only the numeric top-level elapsed_seconds token is normalized; its finite nonnegative float type is checked and all other bytes/fields/types must match.

Each mode also rejects 19 integrity controls and 63 strict schema/semantic controls. The 8 mathematical negative controls are part of the independently replayed finite suite. Malformed/duplicate/nonfinite JSON, Boolean-as-integer substitutions, forged manifests, altered code/results/acceptance/queue, linked/special files, and improperly expanded mathematical scope are rejected. The initial cross-filesystem hardlink-fixture error and its correction are disclosed in PREPARATION_HISTORY.json. The hostile-startup check tests isolated interpreter startup only; it is not misrepresented as another full mathematical replay.

Published preparation receipts record the pre-freeze candidate. A further complete final-delivery run authenticates every final member, including those receipts and ACCEPTANCE, with the fixed external bootstrap and required actual QUEUE pair. Fresh remote byte readback and final downloaded replay are verified separately. These are finite support checks; the all-n proof and imported-result boundaries are assessed in the mathematical reports.

## External trust pins and reproduction

- Mutation-harness SHA-256: 021491721c98cf7a8a0f8d82d9b977d33db51a9c324f40b39177a27f0f2fb294

With UID/EUID 1000, packet directory 0555 and all files/queue files 0444, run Python with -I -S -B (and optionally -O or -OO), then BOOTSTRAP.py, packet directory, before-QUEUE path and after-QUEUE path. Use the before file from the pinned base commit and the after file actually present in this PR. Publish the independently accepted, unchanged partial audit for 30004018 / OWR-16635-003, Socle Filtrations from Duflo–Serganova Kernels (rank 1070). Exhausted, 5/5 approaches. No sixth approach, complete candidate, full-conjecture counterexample, novelty, priority, or exhaustive openness claim is made. AI-authored and AI-audited, unrefereed; not conventional human peer review or proof-assistant verification.

The credited first-layer equality A_1=S_1 and normalized inclusion S_k⊆A_k are consequences of prior HPS/CS work. The original and independent reports explain the strict objectwise-span versus reduced-class-kernel distinction in gl(1|1), the reverse-DS Levi diagnostic, and the restricted tensor/specialization calculations. None extends those examples to a counterexample or proof of the full target. pull_requests.title: 6900004: full labelled stress partitions determine the graph
pull_requests.body:
The full connected coordinate-sign stress partition of a simple graph on fixed labelled vertices determines its edge set, for every n,d >= 1, with all collisions and deficient affine spans retained. An unordered pair is an edge exactly when its collision diagonal is a union of whole strata. This gives a complete answer to the literal equality formulation of Karpenkov (2018), Problem 4.

The proof combines Panina's known singleton collision detector with elementary positive diagonal transport along a continuous collinear path. Known detector, collinear invariance and stress-equivalence machinery are credited. The bounded priority audit located no earlier exact reconstruction in inspected sources; exhaustive novelty and unwritten author intent are not certified.

Arbitrary ambient/abstract equivalence, generic-only and collision-free comparisons, and pure-condition reconstruction are outside this result. The paper includes nonisomorphic path/star graphs with ambient-linearly equivalent full stratifications to make this boundary checkable.

Published preprint and source/verification package: [DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23331540](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23331540). Both files and all metadata were verified with the repository Zenodo tool; the DOI resolves. The requested publication tracker has an exact verified entry in row 72.

Validation includes independent universal proof derivations, exact diagnostics in normal/-O/-OO modes, six actual defective-source mutations in every mode, source and priority audits, PDF visual inspection, and three NEW adversarial whole-package review rounds. The final round found no actionable concerns after two P3 documentation repairs. ## Disposition and exact scope

Accepted scoped partial results for 30001092 / OWR-2487-003. The full source target remains unresolved by this work at 5/5 substantive approaches. The exact question asks for two essentially free p.m.p. actions of one countable group on standard atomless probability spaces, one with an FI orbit relation and one without. There is no global ergodicity hypothesis. The literal catalogue omission of freeness is not used to broaden the category.

## Accepted mathematics and boundaries

Read the unchanged complete authored/SCOPED_RESULTS.md, audit/AUDIT_REPORT.md and audit/CONTEXTUAL_SUPPLEMENT.md, together with authored/EXACT_STATEMENT_AND_SOURCES.md and audit/SCOPE_ACCEPTANCE.md. All 11 authored files and the separate public audit seal are preserved byte-for-byte. The independent review found no substantive defect. The supplement clarifies existing arguments and source attribution without changing any frozen conclusion or hypothesis.

- The quotient construction is a nonfree false positive; taking a diagonal product repairs freeness but destroys its FI certificate.
- Inessentiality uses a Borel complete section partitioned into invariant pieces with equality of the restricted relations, modulo invariant null sets. Completeness need not mean full measure; invariant slicings and smooth connectors remain inessential.
- The canonical infinite-factor-support criterion, recurrence and countable-mixture result retain their aperiodic p.m.p. hypotheses. Non-FI ergodic extraction disintegrates one fixed splitting. No selection among varying decompositions, nor FI-almost-every-ergodic-component converse, is asserted.
- The locally orbit-bijective direction is FI extension implies FI factor. Its contrapositive gives non-FI factor implies non-FI extension. No blanket upward FI transfer or common-product ergodicity is asserted.
- Finite-index induction and finite-normal-quotient reduction retain their stated directions. Reverse transport is proved for a split finite direct factor only. These operations require a seed; infinite-index counting induction is not a probability action.
- The conditional Z-cocycle FI theorem requires a countable nonamenable group Gamma, Hom(Gamma,Z)=0, a free ergodic p.m.p. action on a standard atomless probability space, and superrigidity for every measurable Z-cocycle of that action. It supplies no mixed pair.
- TW arXiv:2410.11754v3 Lemma 5.1 requires ergodicity and supplies a full-domain aperiodic amenable free factor. Connes–Feldman–Weiss supplies its generator without requiring factor ergodicity. The full-domain generator, measurable free-product cocycle extension and probability-level-set contradiction retain their exact assumptions.
- The Peterson–Sinclair obstruction is to the stronger U_fin-superrigid Bernoulli route, not Z-only superrigidity for arbitrary actions. The strong-treeability exclusions require essential freeness, aperiodicity and the cited essential-decomposition theorem; ordinary group indecomposability is insufficient.

The full target is neither solved by a verified mixed pair nor excluded by a general impossibility theorem. ## Accepted result and published preprint

The exact rational binary-input interpretation of Conforti's Problem 1 (OWR51/2008 pp.2904–2905, catalogue30001102/OWR-2489-008) is resolved: polynomial-time exact linear optimization, strong separation and membership in the actual closed convex hull of arbitrary bipartite mixed-integer covers, including boundary queries.

[Published preprint and complete source/verification package](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23352246) · [Zenodo record](https://zenodo.org/records/23352246). The requested Google tracker has the verified details in row80 of gid1254632077.

Arbitrary rational edge demands, unrestricted variable signs and any selected integer coordinates are allowed; graph, dimensions and denominators vary. Total binary input includes objective and rational query. The proof provides an attained exact optimum or a polynomial-bit integral improving ray, denominator-independent short integer labels, an exact LP value oracle with uniformly bounded encodings, an explicit ring-domain interface, closedness of the actual hull and a polynomial facet-encoding bound for the GLS strong interface.

The separate subtree-hull Conjecture2, arbitrary unencoded real-query models, strongly polynomial total complexity, compact extended formulations and an executable full polynomial LP/SFM/GLS implementation are unaddressed.

## Mathematical, source and priority acceptance

Root deductions and two independent mathematical families passed. The total is zero instead of two in the historical OWR14/2011 Conjecture4 k=1 smooth-complex p-adic interpretation. The same example contradicts FLO Conjecture6.12 and the unrestricted local unitary Jacquet converse; it does not contradict generic or tempered positive results.

FLO supplies the complete period bases, normalization, functional equations and adjacent-label exclusion. JPSS supplies segment L-factors; Lapid-Minguez supplies classification, ladder-side matching, involution and prior kernel transport. Gurevich-Ma-Mitra and Mitra-Offen-Sayag supply earlier imprimitive negative-distinction and quotient-descent antecedents for different subgroups. Beuzart-Plessis and Lu-Matringe receive credit for established generic/tempered results; Sharma for a different five-segment combinatorial comparison.

## Accepted result and published preprint **Original-ball paths in Teichmüller space: an elementary corollary of Lenzhen–Rafi**, Alec Kriebel. Published paper and verification package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23430475 (https://zenodo.org/records/23430475).

An explicitly expository original-ball path corollary of Lenzhen–Rafi’s established uniform quasiconvexity theorem. For each fixed closed oriented surface of genus at least two, every pair of points in any original closed half-log Teichmüller ball has a continuous rectifiable path inside that same ball with length at most its ambient distance plus 4c_g. One finite topology-dependent c_g works for all centers, radii and pairs. Radial endpoint retreat followed by a minimizing segment gives the deduction and an affirmative derivation of Farb’s Question 3.5 from prior geometry.

All substantive Teichmüller estimates are credited to Lenzhen–Rafi. ## Accepted scope

Existing published results refute KP-1.64(a), the canonical induced double-contact-cover Stein-fillability implication to transverse quasipositivity. They also refute the twofold slice-Bennequin-sharpness implication in (c), and hence any blanket version of (c) allowing order two.

The positive transverse closure of b6 = (sigma1 sigma2)^6 sigma1^5 sigma2^-21 is a knot with exponent sum -4 and self-linking -7. Its canonical induced cyclic double contact branched cover is Stein fillable. A separate Hayden/generalized-Jones argument proves that its entire oriented smooth knot type is nonquasipositive. Since 2g4(K)-1 >= -1 > -7, its slice-Bennequin inequality is strictly unsharp.

Clause (b), whose hypothesis is a Stein-fillable induced cyclic cover for some n > 2, is not settled by the inspected sources or this audit. ## Direct certificate of an established tensorization failure

This edition records a complete direct proof and full mathematical audit for problem 30004587 / OWR-4990370-005. Ordinary logarithmic-mean GE(1,∞) holds for the normalized qubit depolarizing semigroup and the identity semigroup on a second qubit, but fails for their tensor product.

The underlying amplification failure is prior work. [Brannan–Gao–Junge, Advances in Mathematics 394 (2022), 108129](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10355667), §4.4, in the paragraph immediately before Proposition 4.21, explicitly establishes GE((I−τ₂)⊗id_M₂)<1 using a Bell-state construction. The same statement already appears in [arXiv:2007.06138v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.06138v2). The unamplified qubit estimate GE(1,∞) is established by [Münch–Wirth–Zhang, arXiv:2401.05179v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05179v1), Theorem 3.23 and Remark 3.24. Together with the identity factor's zero derivation, these results already imply the failure at issue. This is an explicit direct certificate and reconstruction of that consequence, not a claim of a new counterexample or mechanism.

The manuscript independently proves the factor estimate for all complex observables, all densities and all times. It then verifies the ambient tensor differential calculus and gives a positive definite rational density and rational self-adjoint observable at t=log 2. The strict comparison reduces to 81>75. ## Result and scope

Every full-dimensional d-polytope with n ≥ d+2 vertices is the coordinate projection of a full-dimensional inscribed (d+1)-polytope with exactly n vertices. The explicit sign choice handles possible affine degeneracy, and radial exposure gives the exact vertex count. Projection monotonicity yields F_d(n) ≤ I_(d+1)(n). ## Mathematical disposition

Problem **30000114**, rank **1217**, alias **OWR-741-008**: **accepted rigorous restricted progress, Approach 1 of 5**. The unrestricted weakened Wills inequality remains unresolved by this work. This is neither a full proof nor a counterexample to the target.

For every n>=2 there is a dimension-only A_n such that every compact convex K and every primitive integer normal a satisfy

    G(K) <= V_n(K) + V_(n-1)(K)/||a||
            + A_n (floor(w_a(K))+1) sum_(i=0)^(n-2) V_i(K).

This controls each fixed bounded-lattice-width class and, by classical flatness, hollow bodies. The lattice-hull reduction also controls every lower-dimensional hull. The proof retains arbitrary translations, boundary lattice planes, lower-rank slices and the sharper surface coefficient for degenerate bodies.

Any sequence whose normalized target residual diverges must have lattice width tending to infinity. The exact unimodular shear shows that its Euclidean inradius need not diverge. The height-one-pyramid example refutes only a stronger coefficientwise Ehrhart estimate: the nonnegative surface deficit Delta(P)=V_(n-1)(P)-g_(n-1)(P) is essential, and the pyramid is not a counterexample to weakened Wills.

The remaining problem is a shape-uniform lower-Ehrhart-sum bound in each fixed dimension over full-dimensional lattice polytopes of unbounded lattice width, retaining Delta(P). The fixed-polytope asymptotics and o(surface) results do not supply it.

A complete attributed proof that ordinary conservative chip-firing HALTING is NP-complete under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions on finite loopless simple strongly connected digraphs with nonnegative binary configurations. Hardness holds with polynomial numerical total initial chips and a specified root whose deletion leaves an acyclic graph with no path of two arcs. The main construction permits antiparallel arcs; a separately proved oriented construction forbids them. The proof includes actual legal checkpoints, conservation, schedule-independent least action, polynomial output bounds, all preprocessing cases and a polynomial-bit NP certificate.

pull_requests.body:
## Accepted result and published preprint

Accepted as a full affirmative answer to Tunçel’s original 2017 existential problem (OWR14/2017, p.799, Open Problem1). The one-sided algebraic regular cone K={x,y,z≥0:xy²≥z³} has the parameter-100 normal barrier F=-25 log(z(xy²-z³)), with D³F(a)[h,u,u]≤0 for every interior base point, cone direction h and real test vector u. No homogeneous polynomial in the original R³ defines K as its hyperbolicity cone.

Published research note and source/verification package: **[10.5281/zenodo.23440119](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23440119)**. The exact reviewed files and metadata were verified on Zenodo, and the DOI resolves. Google Workspace tracker entry `'Math Puzzles'!A151:D151` was appended and read back exactly.

The cone is credited to [Hildebrand, Theorem3.2 family5](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.4814); [Roy–Xiao, Theorem2](https://optimization-online.org/2018/01/6441/) already supplies a different parameter-3 self-concordant barrier on this same cone. The parameter100 is deliberately nonoptimal. The accepted contribution is the explicit negative-curvature certificate together with the arbitrary-polynomial hyperbolicity obstruction. The broader every-regular-cone barrier question is outside the theorem. No worldwide novelty or priority certification is claimed.

The frozen proof was independently reconstructed and reproduced by separate curvature and geometry/barrier/algebraic-boundary adversaries. Both reviewers independently rederived the mathematics, tested adverse controls, verified every archive/metadata binding, recompiled the distributed TeX, and visually checked all five pages; rebuilt text and page pixels matched the frozen PDF. No mathematical repair was required.

AI tools were used extensively in solving, verification and writing. This is **unrefereed**; adversarial AI review is not external human peer review, journal acceptance or proof-assistant certification.

## Scoped counterexample, original question unresolved

The normal singular quadric threefold X = V(x0*x3 − x1*x2) in complex P^4
has numerical surface space R^2, but its positive cone of integral
Ottem-ample surfaces is exactly R_{>0}(1,1), which is not open in that
full space. The same ray occurs with only smooth or lci generators.
Requiring smooth generators does not make the ambient variety smooth.
The counterexample has codimension one.

codimension-one criterion: for a normal integral projective T over C of
dimension at least two, the cone generated by all integral ample
codimension-one centers is the image of Amp(T) in the numerical divisor
cycle space, and is open there exactly when the Cartier-to-Weil map is
surjective. This general criterion does not impose smooth generators.

projective manifolds. This example refutes a broader singular-projective

pull_requests.title: 30005461: Motzkin threshold limit 3 and credited mixed odd SOS powers
pull_requests.body:
## Full two-clause mathematical resolution

For arbitrary real polynomials p,q, if p^(2i+1) and q^(2j+1) are sums
of squares, then (p+q)^(2i+2j+1) is a sum of squares. This is the
published Blekherman–Kozhasov–Reznick theorem, with the truncated-binomial
ingredient credited to Iosif Pinelis. The full credited proof, both source
index/display corrections, arbitrary-degree reduction and edge cases are
included.

For f_c=x^4*y^2+x^2*y^4+1-c*x^2*y^2, every fixed real c<3 has all
sufficiently large odd powers SOS, and the thresholds satisfy lim c_k=3.
The complete argument applies Scheiderer's published Corollary 4.2 to a
strictly positive quadratic section on the integral singular cubic ABC=D^3,
lifts all square-root sections with the cubic hypersurface exact sequence,
and substitutes (A,B,C,D)=(x^2*y,x*y^2,z^3,x*y*z). It gives the exact
Motzkin power without a multiplier or denominator. All sign patterns,
singular boundary points, exponent parity, base points and the limit are
checked explicitly in the proof and substantive independent audit.

Blekherman–Kozhasov–Reznick, Theorem 5.3:
https://doi.org/10.1017/fms.2026.10221
Scheiderer, Corollary 4.2:
https://doi.org/10.1007/s00229-011-0484-3

## Accepted PARTIAL result

Problem 30000374 / OWR-1116-002 remains unresolved by this work. This edition includes the complete authored proof and full substantive independent internal AI mathematical audit. No mathematical correction was required; the proof is byte-identical to its accepted frozen original.

For every countable ordinal α ≥ 2, the related-pair set and a fixed upward section are analytic-complete and non-Borel under the conventional continuous many-one reductions from Baire space, equivalently zero-dimensional Polish source spaces. Color inclusion gives continuous preorder reductions for α ≤ β. Set completeness is not analytic preorder universality: the latter requires one Borel map preserving and reflecting all ordered pairs. ## Accepted partial result: quadratic local-cycle packing

Adds the authored corrected mathematical report, substantive independent internal AI audit, exact source-scope correction, acceptance, and permitted public source metadata for problem 30002668 / OWR-13110-017.

Every general-position arrangement with n red, n blue and n green lines has Omega(n²) pairwise vertex-disjoint properly colored dual four-cycles. General position excludes parallel pairs and triple concurrence. For M differently colored crossings, the exact packing bound is M²/(M + sum_f d(f)²). The planar zone theorem gives sum_f d(f)² <= (C_z+4)N², counting bounded and unbounded faces with their genuine boundary edges. At N=3n and M=3n² this gives at least n²/(C+1/3) disjoint cycles, where C=C_z+4 is absolute.

For problem 30001214 / OWR-3397-002, the unrestricted maximal-spectrum local-closedness assertion is false: in every integer dimension d >= 4, there is a complex affine integral Poisson algebra A and a maximal ideal m whose symplectic core C(m) is not locally closed in Max A.

## Accepted partial result; full single-orbit conjecture unresolved

With the canonical minimal slope-adapted reference lattice and the stated GL_h minuscule data, every Dieudonne lattice has a unique smallest minimal hull. A cyclic sublattice with the same hull yields the complete colength formula C = sum_i (m_i−1)(n_i−1)/2 + sum_{i<j} m_i n_j, with factors ordered by increasing slope and repeated copies included. If the interior part is nonzero, d(M) <= C and d(M)=C exactly when a(M)=1. Thus the entire a-number-one locus is saturated under invariant-function strata and their J-orbits.

The full single J-orbit assertion when there are multiple distinct interior slopes remains unresolved. Hull and colength do not determine the full invariant function. pull_requests.body:
## Accepted partial result; exact target unresolved

Problem 30001551 / OWR-4425-006 asks whether exactly three independent constant-free equations on three variables, with nonempty variable words on both sides, admit one common nonperiodic solution in a finite-alphabet free monoid. Empty variable images are allowed; independence concerns the complete solution set.

This unrefereed AI-assisted exposition and independent internal AI mathematical/source/computational audit accept three partial statements:

- At most one equation of a hypothetical independent triple with a common nonperiodic solution admits an erasing deletion witness.
- If the triple has a common erasing nonperiodic solution, no equation admits an erasing deletion witness.
- A balanced three-variable system with a common nonperiodic solution and a member equivalent to pairwise commutation is equivalent to at most two original members.

The complete proof and substantive audit are preserved. The exact supplied clarification patch is applied: the two-word criterion uses injectivity of an indexed morphism on distinct formal letters, correctly covering equal and empty images; the three-profile heading explicitly concerns nonperiodic erasing morphisms. No theorem, hypothesis, or inference changes.

pull_requests.body:
## Accepted theorem; combined target only partially resolved

For problem 30003650, this edition preserves the complete proof of p_n^+=p_n for every n>=1, including singular matrices with finite strictly positive factorizations. It also proves P_(n,r)^+=P_(n,r) on every exact ordinary-matrix-rank stratum 1<=r<=n. Both maxima are attained. The convention is A=BB^T with an n by p factor B; every entry of a positive factor is strictly positive.

The combined two-question target is ACCEPT_AS_PARTIAL. Its maximum-gap question g_n=max(cp^+(A)-cp(A)) remains undetermined in general. The result does not supply explicit ordinary maxima p_n in every order, and does not assert equality of the two ranks for every individual matrix. No novelty is claimed.

The self-contained proof uses finite conic reduction, closedness of bounded ordinary-CP-rank sets by a trace-bounded factor argument, and two invertible congruences. Positive congruence gives attained positive-factor witnesses without decreasing the ordinary CP-rank for sufficiently small parameters. Negative congruence preserves a given positive factor on the explicit interval 0<t<=alpha/2, and its strictly positive inverse pulls a minimal nonnegative factor back to a positive factor. Removing zero columns is essential. Both congruences preserve ordinary rank, with no extension of an ambient-interior theorem to singular boundary points.

The retained bounds are g_1=g_2=g_3=0, 0<=g_4<=1 and 1<=g_n<=p_n-3 for n>=5. Low-order equality and gap-one witnesses are attributed to Bomze–Dickinson–Still. The rank-r bound is P_(n,r)-r; the positive-definite bound p_n-n is not claimed for all singular matrices. Row duplication shows g_n is nondecreasing but does not determine it.

The main sources are the [Dickinson contribution to Oberwolfach Report 52/2017](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46715), [Bomze–Dickinson–Still's complete author manuscript dated November 4, 2014](https://api.newton.ac.uk/website/v0/events/preprints/NI14088), its [2015 journal record](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.laa.2015.05.021), and [Lai–Yoshise's 2022 published paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10589-022-00417-4). ## Accepted partial results; exact conjecture unresolved

Problem 30000879 / OWR-1738-004 asks whether a torsion-free nilpotent group G of finite integral cohomological dimension n, with a class α in H²(G,C×), has a subgroup H on which α vanishes and for which gldim(CH) = gldim(C^αG) = r. This unrefereed AI-assisted exposition and independent internal AI mathematical/source/computational audit preserve the complete accepted proofs and substantive audit:

For Karpenkov's historical eight-sail Klein model, this unrefereed AI-assisted manuscript proves countably infinitely many GL(3,Z)-inequivalent continued fractions in every fixed totally real cubic field. Its independent internal AI mathematical, source, and computational audit found no required mathematical correction.

- The actual eight-sail union recovers the defining hyperplanes, their rational multiplication algebra, and an integral multiplier order. The recovered-order trace discriminant is geometric and must not be confused with an operator-polynomial discriminant.
- The lattices Z + f O_K have invariant f⁴ disc(K), proving pairwise inequivalence for all positive integers f. Every full lattice has an irreducible positive-eigenvalue SL(3,Z) realization.

## Accepted partial theorem; unrestricted singleton problem unresolved

For strictly increasing positive integer moduli n_i, one canonical forbidden residue 0 <= a_i < n_i, and inclusive activation m >= n_i, the survivor set has logarithmic density whenever, outside a reciprocal-summable exceptional family, the residues satisfy one of finitely many fixed identities q a_i = p n_i + c with integer q >= 1, p, c. The density equals the decreasing limit of the finite-periodic survivor densities. Coprimality, disjointness, bounded residues, and reciprocal summability of the patterned family are unnecessary. Natural density of the infinite survivor set is not asserted.

In the fully patterned class, arbitrary finite positive per-modulus activation thresholds preserve this logarithmic density. The summable exceptional family retains the original activation condition. The audit's explicit counterexample rejects extending threshold invariance to arbitrary summable exceptions; it is not a counterexample to the theorem or to the unrestricted original target.

## Accepted partial theorem; factorial-minus-one irrationality unresolved

Let H_N = sum_{n=2}^N 1/(n!-1), let Q_N be its positive reduced denominator, and let S be the infinite sum. The complete elementary proof establishes:

1. limsup log(Q_N)/(N^(3/2) log N) >= 1/3.
2. For every fixed 0 < c < 1/3, the set A_c = {N >= 2: log Q_N >= c N^(3/2) log N} has lower asymptotic density at least 1/2.
3. Q_N(S-H_N) tends to positive infinity through A_c.

This is a reduced-denominator result, not merely an unreduced-lcm bound. It rests on the reciprocal-sum cancellation lemma P | D G^2, a factorial-gap estimate, exact terminal-block/prefix divisibility, the asymptotic constant, and residue-class chains in fourth-power intervals. ## Prior harmonic corollary; weighted convergence unsupplied

For A contained in (1,infinity), suppose |kx-y| >= 1 for every ordered pair of distinct elements and every positive integer k. Then H_A(X) = sum_{x in A, x <= X} 1/x = o(log X), and consequently sum_{x in A, x < n} 1/x = o(log n) along integers.

This is a known consequence of [Koukoulopoulos, Lamzouri and Lichtman (2025), Theorem 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09539v1). The research theorem is explicitly imported and is not independently reproved. The full elementary application, complete hypothesis audit, historical formulation reconciliation and acceptance report are retained. Unit separation supplies the exact discreteness convention; failure of the nonnegative harmonic little-o limit gives positive upper harmonic density; tolerance 1 gives the strict contradiction for distinct elements and a positive integer multiplier. Closed and strict integer cutoffs differ by at most 1/n.

The weighted-convergence question, sum_{x in A} 1/(x log x) < infinity, is not supplied or attempted. The summation-by-parts boundary is preserved. The full two-part problem is not classified as solved. No novelty, new harmonic theorem, stronger universal counting-density or Behrend-rate estimate, or current worldwide openness claim is made.

pull_requests.title: 20000970: audited exact simplicial-core parking sampler partial
pull_requests.body:
## Accepted scoped partial result; general efficient sampling unresolved

For finite connected undirected simple graphs with a prescribed retained root,
nonroot simplicial deletion has constant fibers of size equal to the deleted
vertex's degree. Uniform valid core orientations and independent exactly
uniform neighbor-label pivots give an exact sampler for rooted acyclic
orientations and, by the correspondence as presented by Benson, Chakrabarty
and Tetali, maximal parking functions. The complete substantive proof and
independent mathematical audit are retained; no blocking correction was found.

The result gives a 2^b times polynomial exact fallback in the number b of edges
of the computed residual core, exact equality of total-variation error for
valid core laws with independent uniform pivots and a certificate fixed
independently of sampling randomness, and a self-contained polynomial-time
chordal specialization. The low-level helpers assume a valid root-preserving
simplicial-deletion plan; this edition adds that optional documentation contract
without changing the algorithm.

The probability theorem requires an ideal independent-fair-bit interface.
Fair-bit rejection terminates almost surely with expected cost; sparse hashing
has its stated expected-cost interpretation; final output sorting adds
O(m log(m+1)), and arbitrary-precision costs are retained. SystemRandom is an
implementation choice, and seeded PRNG tests do not certify physical entropy.

## Corrected partial results; general two-set question unresolved

For every 3-permutable set S and every fixed integer C >= 0, only finitely many positive integers n have the whole integer interval [n,2n-C] contained in S. Here 3-permutable requires an omega enumeration avoiding both increasing and decreasing 3-term arithmetic progressions at arbitrary subsequence positions. The complete proof gives the equivalent divergent-deficit conclusion, the P >= k+2 finite-prefix bound for k distinct C3 scales and two fixed anchors, and the stated bounded-additive-dyadic-run and monochromatic-interval exclusions.

For each prescribed nondecreasing unbounded f:N->N, an adaptation of Geneson's construction yields one 3-permutable set with upper natural density at least 2/3 and infinitely many full intervals with positive deficits at most f of their starts. Those deficits still diverge. The proof also gives translation equivalence of the zero-based and positive-integer two-set existence questions. ## Scoped prior result and endpoint audit

For Ball 2002 Problem 4 / 2000004 / AMR-019-0004, this draft credits the Almi–Krömer–Molchanova Lavrentiev-gap result in its exact two-component Ciarlet–Nečas setting. The accepted ranges are d=2 with p>2 and 1<q<p/(p−2), and d=3 with 3<p<4 and 2<q<p/(p−2). The homogeneous polyconvex energy forces continuity; both comparison classes have the same partial Dirichlet data and CN constraint.

The prior source is [A new example for the Lavrentiev phenomenon in nonlinear elasticity](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00033-023-02132-4), ZAMP 75, article 2 (2024). The inspected versions are the publisher PDF and [arXiv:2309.08288v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.08288v2), revised 8 November 2023. Existence, finite-distortion, change-of-variables and topological results remain external cited dependencies; their deep proofs were not independently reconstructed.

### Two-dimensional endpoint qualification

The logarithmic competitor printed after (3.9) in arXiv pages 10–11 and publisher page 9 has infinite inverse-Jacobian energy at q=p/(p−2). The exact lower-triangular determinant is J=A t^(alpha+beta−1)(alpha L+1)/L^4. At the endpoint it gives J^(−q) comparable above and below to t^(−1)L^(3q), whose reference-coordinate integral diverges. Both printed logarithmic denominator powers are preserved. This is a failed construction/proof step, not a disproof of the endpoint theorem. The strict-range 2D and 3D arguments do not use that endpoint construction.

The complete authored theorem summary, source/hypothesis audit, endpoint/proof notes and bounded acceptance are retained. The proof notes include the normalized distortion term W(I)|Omega_s| and the integrated positive-part/Hölder repair with coefficient 2^(1−p). Remark 3.1 does not supply the missing connector estimates or preserve boundary-only constraints by itself. The bounded correction search on 10 October 2026 found no repair; it was not exhaustive. pull_requests.body:
## Variable-base universal extension refuted; fixed base 2 unresolved

This prose-only edition retains the complete substantive proof and independent
mathematical audit. No mathematical correction was required. The combined
problem is not declared solved.

Let P(X)=X^4-X^3-X^2-X-1, let gamma be its unique positive root, and define
c=1/((gamma-1)P'(gamma)), alpha=2c gamma^20, and beta=gamma alpha.
Then 1.92<gamma<1.93 and alpha/beta=1/gamma is irrational. Every indexed
term floor(alpha gamma^n) and floor(beta gamma^n), for n>=0, is even.
Every positive odd integer is omitted from finite sums of distinct positions.
Equal values at different positions remain usable separately and cannot
remove this parity obstruction.

The explicit trace recurrence has residue 1/3. Exact root/coefficient bounds
imply |E_m|<3(5/6)^m<1/6 for every m>=20, giving strict floor endpoints.
The shift 20 covers both exponent-zero terms. The historical independent
check also isolates the unshifted m=3 floor as the odd integer 1, emphasizing
why an unproved eventual-to-all-positions step would be invalid.

The original hypotheses permit beta=gamma alpha for irrational gamma.
At gamma=2 the corresponding ratio is rational and inadmissible. Therefore
this counterexample addresses the universal extension to 1<gamma<2;
it does not resolve the original fixed-base-2 question or classify all bases.
Original formulations and indexed-sum definitions were historically checked in
[Graham (1971), question 12, printed page 36](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/71_08_integer_sums.pdf)

pull_requests.body:
## Accepted partial results; full absolute-bound target unresolved

For B_n=binom(2n,n), let f(n)=sum 1/p over primes p<=n with p not dividing B_n.
This prose-only edition preserves the complete substantive mathematical proof
and independent audit. No substantive mathematical correction was required.

- Exact valuation, digit and residue criteria characterize nondivisibility.
- The contribution at n=q^r rules out every summable all-n envelope depending
  only on shell depth, even after deleting any fixed finite prime set.
- Testing only L(n)=o(log n) common carry levels gives an unbounded relaxation.
  For each fixed c>0, testing floor(c log(2n)) levels differs from f by at most
  the reciprocal sum of the finitely many odd primes p<exp(1/c).
- For every fixed r, F_r(n) tends along all integers to
  2^(-r) log(1+1/r), derived from Sander's published exponential-sum estimate.
  Constants and thresholds may depend on r; no uniformity or infinite-sum
  interchange is claimed.
- With c0=sum_{k>=2} log(k)/2^k, the EGRS first moment gives liminf f(n)=c0.
  The prime-3 subsequence gives liminf f(3^m)>=c0+1/3, and the published EGRS
  two-base theorem strengthens this to limsup f(n)>=c0+8/15.

construction does not produce actual simultaneous nondivisibility. Deep-shell

## Partial density theorem; both universal targets unresolved

This prose-only edition retains the complete substantive proof and independent
mathematical audit. For n>=5, let F(n) be the maximum of m+p(m) over composites
4<=m<n, with p(m) the least prime divisor. For every fixed real K, the integers
with F(n)-n<=K have natural density zero. Thus F(n)-n tends to infinity in
natural density. Neither eventual positivity for all sufficiently large n
nor pointwise divergence is established. A density-zero set is not proved
finite, and no global last exception is claimed.

The self-contained proof derives Var(S)<=Hv for reduced-residue counts modulo
even squarefree Q directly from CRT joint probabilities, nonnegative divisor
expansion, a triangular-sum bound, and exact Euler-product cancellation.
It neither assumes independence nor requires H<Q. Elementary product bounds
and prime density zero give the composite-witness transfer. The density limit
is taken with H and Q fixed; only afterward is H enlarged.

obstruction at primorial multiples, endpoint/parity reductions, the correct
square-root upper bound, the exact prime-square identities

## Accepted partial theorem; exact asymptotic unresolved

For the classical Hofstadter consecutive-sum sequence with seed (1,2), each
later term is the least integer strictly greater than its predecessor that is
a sum of at least two consecutive earlier terms. The accepted theorem gives,
for every integer n>=2, with all logarithms natural,

    a_n-n >= (log(log(n))-log(log(5)+log(2)/3))/log(4).

The finite plateau lemma gives V<Q<=2*T^2*(T-1)^2<2*T^4 for any
constant-deviation interval 3<=r<=s, where T=a_r, V=a_s and Q is the least
2*4^k strictly above T^2*(T-1)^2/2. This subfamily of powers makes 8Q a square;
the positive one-sided crossing error is excluded by a difference of squares.
The all-index threshold recurrence handles skipped levels and nonempty
plateaus and starts at M(0)=5. No mathematical correction was required.

pull_requests.body:
## Accepted corrected prior theorem; coefficient one unresolved

For one absolute C>0 and infinitely many positive integers n, the complete
corrected proof establishes

    omega(n-k) <= Omega(n-k) <= C log k,  for every integer 2<=k<n.

Here omega counts distinct factors, Omega counts with multiplicity, and log
is natural. Credit is given to Cheuk Fung (Joshua) Lau, *On the Number of
Prime Factors of Consecutive Integers*, [arXiv:2604.15042v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15042v2),
24 June 2026, Theorem 1.3. This is an authored proof correction and audit of
that prior result, with no novelty or whole-problem resolution claim.

With N=n-1 and epsilon=1/(C log 2), every positive integer m<N satisfies
m+epsilon*Omega(m)<=N, hence m+epsilon*omega(m)<=N, for infinitely many N.
The same one positive epsilon works throughout. The closest endpoint uses
k=2, not the excluded k=1. No explicit numerical C or epsilon is certified.
The original distinct-prime weak-inequality formulation was checked in
[Erdos, Some unconventional problems in number theory, Acta 33 (1979),
printed p.71](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-23.pdf).

Coefficient one remains unresolved. The logarithmic result controls it only
beyond a fixed cutoff, leaving a finite terminal window of simultaneous
inequalities at infinitely many witnesses. The epsilon transfer does not
eliminate that obligation for coefficient one.

pull_requests.body:
## Accepted prior fixed-r matching order

The prior STARFLEET Math result for Erdős Problem 538 is accepted as a
conventional mathematical proof. For every fixed integer r>=2,

    E_r(N)=Theta_r(log N/log log N).

E_r(N) maximizes S(A)=sum_{a in A}1/a over positive a<=N, with at most r
ordered pairs (p,a), p prime, a in A, m=pa, for every integer m.
The cap includes products above N. Arbitrary admissible sets need not be
squarefree; squarefreeness is used only in the constructed lower witnesses.
This is an audit of a prior public claim, credited to STARFLEET Math, with
no novelty claim.

The accepted finite inequalities are

    log(log(N+1)) S(A) <= 2r(1+log(N^2)), for r>=2 and N>=2,
    log(N+1) <= 4+8192(ell(N)+1) S(A_N), for every natural N,

where A_N has global cap two. Put L(0)=0, L(N)=floor(log_2 N) for N>=1,
and ell(N)=floor(log_2 L(N)) when L(N)>=1, otherwise ell(N)=0.
All unsubscripted logarithms are natural. No real logarithm of zero occurs.
The lower witness also applies to every cap r>=2. No sharp finite extremum,
sharp leading constant or matching growing-r dependence is established.

## Attributed prior bounds; uniform exponent-one upper question unresolved

This prose-only edition preserves the complete authored derivations and acceptance of three prior works on distinct multiples in intervals. Define f(n,m) as the least length H for which (m,m+H] contains distinct multiples of 1,...,n; F(n)=max_m f(n,m); h_P(n) is the prime-only maximum. All logarithms are natural.

- Wouter van Doorn's published theorem gives F(n)-f(n,n)>0.36 n log n/log log n eventually.
- Scott Duke Kominers's arXiv:2607.10431v1 gives liminf [F(n)-f(n,n)]/(n log n)>=1/e.
- Kaizhe Chen and Samuel Korsky's arXiv:2607.26450v2 gives F(n)<=n^(4/3) exp(O(log n/log log n)), h_P(n)<<n^(4/3)/(log n)^(1/3), and F(n)>=h_P(n)>=n exp(((log 2)/2-o(1))log n/log log n).

The last lower bound and the known diagonal upper estimate imply [F(n)-f(n,n)]/(n log n)->infinity. This is a consequence of the credited prior results, not a new theorem. The uniform upper question F(n)<=n^(1+o(1)) remains unresolved by these results. The fixed-start asymptotic in Erdos Problem 710 is separate and is not settled here. ## Accepted restricted-family result

The full EP-509 question remains unresolved. This edition preserves the complete
authored written proofs and independent audit, with no required mathematical
correction and no claim of novelty, priority, an improved general bound, or a
solution of the unrestricted disk-cover problem. The alias is 2304007 /
AMR-022-4007, Hayman's Problem 4.7.

For every compact planar set with finitely many connected components, the
finite/countable closed-disk covering content equals the minimum sum of
circumradii over partitions of those components. The minimum is attained.
Thus a fixed polynomial's bounds 2+epsilon for every epsilon>0 would imply
an attained bound 2, but no such unrestricted estimate is proved here.

For p(z)=(z-a)^n-c, n>=2 and t=|c|, put b=(t+1)^(1/n). The exact content is b
for 0<=t<=1, and min{b,n[(t+1)^(1/n)-(t-1)^(1/n)]/2} for t>1. Degree one has
content 1. With q_n=(1-2/n)^n, the family maximum is
M_n=[2/(1-q_n)]^(1/n)<2, attained at t=(1+q_n)/(1-q_n).
The proof covers the full closed region, countable covers, and every component
partition, without assuming that an optimal covering has rotational symmetry.

although one shared disk costs less than 6/5. This is a closed-form analytic
route obstruction with the complete exact inequalities retained. It is not a

pull_requests.body:
## Accepted prior original-statement result

The prior EP730 proof is accepted as a conventional mathematical solution:
infinitely many distinct positive n<m have equal prime supports of
binomial(2n,n) and binomial(2m,m). Infinitely many consecutive pairs occur.
This is an audit of prior work, with no new-solution or novelty claim.

As credited by the author's public formalization manifest, Liam Price
provided the informal idea, Tomodovodoo an algebraic follow-up, and Will Blair
the analytic reconstruction/formalization. The author describes review as
self-assessed and the earlier informal argument as unadjudicated. Priority
and unavailable antecedent material were not independently authenticated.

With T=5289, P=42Tx+11, Q=72Tx+13, R=28Tx+5 and S=72Tx+19, the family is

    n(x)=P(x)Q(x)−1=84591927504x²+7076682x+142.

The lower asymptotic density of successful positive parameters x is strictly
greater than 107/2500. This is density in x, not in n or in all pairs. The
positive strictly increasing quadratic makes x -> (n(x),n(x)+1) injective
and completes the original-statement bridge. Equality of prime supports is
not equality of valuations or of central binomial coefficients.

Sources: [Will Blair, complete positive-density proof at the audited pin](https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/f297d710018270c66b296082766334974260bcbc/ErdosProblems/Erdos730/compute/full_density/proof.md),

## Accepted conditional partial result

For an ordinary real-valued additive function f with density-zero strict
decreases, suppose that for one fixed real c the residual f−c log is
approximable by periodic sequences in density. Then f(n)=c log n for every
positive integer, with c≥0. A sufficient condition is
Σ_p min(1,|f(p)−c log p|)/p<∞. Values at higher prime powers may be arbitrary
finite real numbers; complete additivity is not assumed.

The complete written proof uses a bounded arctangent transform, vanishing
mean variation, fixed-period averaging without a period-dependent loss,
tightness excluding either endpoint, and fixed coprime-dilation witnesses.
The prime-tail argument treats large-prime squares and finite-small-prime
valuation truncation separately, with the order of limits explicit.
Two lifting lemmas and all mathematical boundary examples are retained.
Absolute o(1) logarithmic approximation off o(X) exceptions already suffices,
even when its slope and offset vary with X, because the offset cancels.

The unrestricted EP 1122 / 2503 problem remains unresolved by this work.
Density-zero decreases alone have not been shown to imply the periodic
residual premise, the sufficient prime-tail condition, or absolute

pull_requests.title: 3100034: audit prior balanced-permutation classification
pull_requests.body:
## Accepted prior resolution

This authored exposition records the exact finite balanced-subsequence-pattern
classification proved by Gal Beniamini, Nir Lavee and Nati Linial in
[*How Balanced Can Permutations Be?*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00493-024-00127-x),
Combinatorica 45, article 9 (2025). For integers n>=k>=1:

- k=1: every n>=1.
- k=2: n>=2 and n=0 or 1 modulo 4.
- k=3: n>=3 and n=0,1,9,20,28,29 modulo 36.
- k>=4: no n>=k.

This is an audit of a prior published resolution, with no novelty claim.
The pattern definition uses arbitrary increasing index sets. Endpoints,
infinitude for each k<=3, and nonexistence for each k>=4 are included.

## Complete proof and finite-evidence boundary

The elementary increasing-pair square identity gives the positive discrepancy
n(n-1)(2n+5)/72 and a complete contradiction for n>=k>=4. Downward closure,
its endpoints, and elementary order-1/order-2 sufficiency remain self-contained.
Order-3 arithmetic, quarter-turn counting, the odd-centre correction, six
source-attributed analytical families, chamber cuts, and exact finite-sum
polynomial derivations are retained. Their unbounded conclusions do not rely
on interpolation from sampled values.

Full order-3 sufficiency additionally uses premise F1, the 19 separately

pull_requests.body:
## Accepted restricted result

This authored prose edition proves a sufficient fixed-rank-block criterion
for simultaneous lower and upper matroid degree bounds. For block
incidence κ, one basis satisfies both sides within additive κ−1 and costs
at most L. When κ≤Δ, this gives the requested additive Δ−1 on the stated
restricted class. The same-basis complement reduction is proved fully.

L is the LP optimum AFTER ceiling/floor normalization of rational degree
bounds, not the weaker unrounded rational-bound LP. Original integral
feasibility gives L≤OPT. Finite rational costs can be negative.

Canonical exchange components are the finest fixed-rank blocks and are
pointwise incidence-minimal only in the stated indexed anchor-complement
model retaining every original upper row. This does not exclude pruning,
merging duplicates, linear combinations, face restriction, or other methods.

The tight-face extension uses a direct sum of successive matroid minors.
It returns an original basis costing at most a specified feasible LP point.

restricted guarantee follows. The complete polynomial tight-set preorder

pull_requests.title: 2366 / EP887: audit Czech five-divisor construction; K>=5, general bound unresolved
pull_requests.body:
## Accepted prior construction, with ancillary corrections

This authored edition independently reconstructs the core of Theorem 1 in
M. Czech's pinned July 2026 manuscript. Every positive integral solution of
z²−56x²=65 with x≥37 gives five explicit distinct divisors of
n=(x²−1)(x²−4)(x²−16)(x²−49) in the strictly open right interval
(√n,√n+31 n^(1/4)). A positive Pell recurrence from (37,277) yields
infinitely many distinct n. Any K in the original one-sided uniform-bound
formulation therefore satisfies K≥5. The general EP887 question remains
unresolved by this work.

This is an audit of a prior construction, not a newly claimed theorem.
The complete elementary factorization, positivity, distinctness, strict
window inequalities, finite base cases and infinitude proof are retained.
No external upper-bound theorem, general Pell existence theorem, complete
divisor census, or author-supplied verifier is a proof dependency.

## Corrections and limits

- 31 is the least integer constant for all five displayed divisors at every
  admissible parameter. It is not least among real constants: 30.5 works
  throughout the family. Every C>30 works eventually; C≤30 never contains
  all five displayed divisors. The shifted-polynomial proof and all 26
  small-parameter square exclusions are public.
- Pell necessity applies only to the fifth pair with its prescribed midpoint.
  An explicit off-Pell additional-divisor witness is retained without making
  a complete-census claim.
- The original question is one-sided; a symmetric version changes the
  numerical normalization and is not a general same-window count equality.
- The balanced-split method is shared with the consecutive-factor construction;
  the weight sets are not literal affine recenterings. Exhaustive maximality
  is not asserted from an omitted enumeration.

The nonsquareness argument is retained. Complete sample counts, eventual
exact-five behavior, the incomplete secondary family, speculative sixth-pair
and geometric exclusions, and historical priority or record claims are
outside this edition's accepted conclusions.

## Sources and review status

- M. Czech, [Five divisors near sqrt(n), infinitely often: a Pell-tuned
  refinement of the Erdős–Rosenfeld construction](https://czechu.blog/erdos/problems/887/note887.pdf),

  construction; the printed Proposition 4.1 interval typo is not silently repaired.

## Accepted restricted result

This authored prose edition proves simultaneous proportional edge
factorization for every finite loopless bipartite multigraph whose connected
components each have empty or regular nonempty 2-core. For arbitrary
positive real fractions summing to one, the same partition satisfies every
color's floor/ceiling quota at every original vertex degree. Core degrees
may vary between components, and arbitrary finite trees may be attached.
Parallel edges, forests, bipartite pseudoforests, isolated vertices, the null
graph, and one color are covered. Irregular surviving 2-cores are outside
the sufficient hypothesis. No mathematical correction was required.

## Complete general proofs

The finite quota-word lemma includes its lower-bound circulation reduction
and integral augmenting-flow proof; it uses the original real fractions.
The complete multiplicity-aware core-structure argument and alternating-path
proof of the perfect-matching decomposition are retained. Monotone prefix
counts extend core colors to attachment edges, and one-precolored-edge
completion propagates through trees. Quotas use original degrees throughout.

The fixed-instance rational-cell lemma preserves both integer threshold
equalities and strict inequalities, including zero-degree and zero/one
unfixed-coordinate cases. It gives no bounded-denominator testing guarantee.

## Accepted prior results and exact residual

This authored edition retains the complete repaired proof of Ema Skottová
and Raphael Steiner's 2025 prior result: for every k>=5 and every r>=1,
there exists a finite simple (k,r)-graph. Both appendices, the k=6,8
change-point and two-block bridge, vertex-deletion wraparound, gluing,
sparse critical scaffolds, and all-large-orders allocation are included.
Every correctness-relevant printed repair is explicit. The theorem
statements and parameter thresholds are unchanged. A focused independent
AI audit accepted the repaired proof with no further required correction.

Writing A=8(k-1)(18r+3), the progression orders are n>=A(6r+3)+1 with
n=1 modulo A; every order n>=A[2(k-2)A(6r+3)+2] is covered as well.

pull_requests.body:
## Accepted restricted results

This authored proof/audit edition preserves complete analytical arguments
for weighted edge coloring with arbitrary real weights in [0,1]. The local
parameter b is the maximum optimal unit-bin count at a vertex, not the
ceiling of weighted degree. Adjacent edges may share a feasible color.

Simple forests have exact index b for b>=1. Multigraphs with forest
support, with arbitrary finite parallel multiplicity, admit 2B-1 colors
from supplied feasible local B-bin packings. Taking B=b is existential;
efficient computation of optimal bin packings is not claimed.

A cycle-breaking matching gives B+1 colors for simple cacti, including
non-bipartite ones. If b=1, one color suffices. The retained bipartite
unicyclic family proves the exact worst-case value b+1 for every b>=2.
A separate parallel forest-support family has exact index b+1 for every
b>=2; it attains 2b-1 only at b=2, not at all b.

The complete eleven-edge b=3 construction has exact index four. Its
specified frozen optimal root packing requires five colors to extend,
while recoloring gives four. This is a local-method obstruction, not a
counterexample to the Chung–Ross five-color target for b=3.

Empty graphs have index zero. Nonempty all-zero graphs use one color
under the convention that every edge is assigned. Disconnected components
reuse a palette, isolated vertices impose no constraint, and supplied
packings need not be optimal. All proof steps, parameterized construction
formulas and the full frozen construction are retained.

## Accepted restricted results

For ordinary stable Grothendieck and Schubert polynomials, the skew-sum
factorization uses the same symmetric rectangular factor for both bases.
The Schubert support of a skew sum is exactly the embedded Cartesian
product of the factor supports, and is left-weak convex if and only if
both factors are. The complete polynomial proof, left-weak upper-ideal
and product-interval proof, skew-indecomposable minimal-counterexample
reduction, and parameterized Boolean family from 132 are retained.

The general Schubert-support left-weak convexity conjecture remains
unresolved by this work. No novelty or current-openness claim is made.

The authored example F=S1243-S1342+2 S2341 has the same convex support,
coefficient-sign pattern, unique lowest term, and right-descent restriction
as G1243, yet pi_3 F=S1234+S2314 has a missing interval middle. The full
direct polynomial calculation is included. F is not any Grothendieck
polynomial, so it refutes only a coefficient-blind induction shortcut.
The G2143 example is attributed to Weigandt, Example 1.4. The G13254
right-weak failure is solely a convention check.

correction. The independent historical audit reconstructed all 873

pull_requests.body:
## Restricted result and exact limits

For even lattices of signature (n,2), n >= 3, polynomiality of the full integral-weight, trivial-character orthogonal modular-form ring descends from a finite-index normal subgroup to an overgroup generated by actual linear reflections. The complete equivariant-generator lemmas, affine Spec geometry, effective-action argument, and proof preserving the original modular weights are retained.

Record the complete reconstructed counterexample and mathematical audit for 30000663 / OWR-1452-027. # Sharp modulus range for triangle counts in dense random graphs

For fixed p in (0,1), ordinary triangles T_n counted once in G(n,p), and every positive integer sequence q_n, max over all residues a of |q_n P(T_n = a mod q_n)-1| tends to zero if and only if q_n=o(n^2). ## Credited negative resolution

Publishes the proof reconstruction, mathematical audit, scoped acceptance, and public verification metadata for **2200014 / AMR-021-0014**, Conjecture 9 in Shapiro's polynomial problem list.

The conjecture is false. **Katkova, Shapiro and Vishnyakova (2024)** are credited for the disproof and primitive family in [In search of Newton-type inequalities, Section 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.12200v1#page=20). Their work was published in *Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications* 538(1), article 128349, [DOI 10.1016/j.jmaa.2024.128349](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmaa.2024.128349).

Our exact degree-24 reconstruction is
`R(x) = (38x^2 - 188x + 326) product_{j=1}^{22}(10^6 x + 10^6 + j)`.
It has strictly positive integer coefficients and exactly **22 distinct simple negative real roots**, while the selected weighted-index parity sequence has **at most 20 changes**. This disproves the bound both for distinct roots and for roots counted with multiplicity.

# Explicit Beurling-transform counterexamples in an analytic annihilator

Both endpoint questions in the bilinear analytic annihilator of Hayman and Lingham, Problem 7.72, have negative answers under the printed negative-kernel convention. The norm-one input v(z)=z/bar(z) on the unit disc annihilates every integrable analytic test function, while its Beurling transform is 1+log|z|^2 and is essentially unbounded. Explicit polynomials v_m(z)=z^2 sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-|z|^2)^j lie in the same annihilator, have norm one and have transform norm H_m, the m-th harmonic number. Each fixed polynomial has bounded transform, but no common uniform constant exists.

This is an exposition and independent explicit verification of consequences of classical formulas, with a self-contained proof. Iwaniec published the exact nonpolynomial witness, output and primitive in 1986. Gill published the general positive-angular transform formula in 2010; the polynomial formula and harmonic-number norm follow by elementary specialization. The 2019 Hayman-Lingham book attributes resolution of Problem 7.72 to Volberg. Its cited reference 52 is the 2008 Banuelos-Janakiraman finite-p paper; the current audit did not locate an explicit full-target account there or a separate Volberg proof. ### Complete symbolic common-one-color theorem

Let G be a finite simple graph of maximum degree at most three, with no proper ordinary three-edge-coloring, but with a proper ordinary three-edge-coloring after deletion of every single edge. Give every edge a list of exactly three colors. If the total intersection of the lists is nonempty, then a proper list edge coloring exists if and only if the assignment is nonconstant. Isolated vertices are allowed. There is no graph-order, total-palette or exception-count bound.

The full proof and substantive independent mathematical audit are preserved. A permissible color class of any ordinary deletion coloring covers every degree-three vertex and leaves exactly one odd cycle through the deleted edge. The local overlap of two such critical cycles detects nonconstant reduced two-lists. Color the selected matching with a globally common color, and color the residual paths and cycles from their reduced lists. This unique-odd-cycle assertion is restricted to permissible deletion-derived color classes, not arbitrary matchings covering the degree-three vertices. The constructive procedure uses supplied deletion colorings for at most two incident edges; no efficiency claim is made for finding those colorings.

### Exact fixed-matching criterion and explicit boundaries

For a specified matching M covering every degree-three vertex, the strategy whose common-color class is exactly M succeeds if and only if every odd residual cycle has nonconstant reduced two-lists. This characterizes the fixed-M strategy, not unrestricted full list colorability. It does not assert that a full list coloring uses the common color at every cubic vertex. The complete critical-cycle family is connected under edge intersection; pairwise intersection of all members is not claimed.

An explicit 25-vertex, 37-edge critical graph has a covering matching leaving C3+C3+C19. Thus coverage alone does not imply a unique odd residual cycle. Its 16 covering matchings split into 12 with one odd cycle and four with three; all odd components must satisfy the criterion. A seven-edge one-common-color example has a failed matching choice and an explicit successful full coloring using another matching. These are matching-method boundaries, not counterexamples to list colorability. A printed empty-intersection example is itself colorable, so being outside the theorem is not evidence of uncolorability.

## Accepted partial mathematics; unrestricted target unresolved

This draft records the initial authored edition for problem 3251 / Open Problem Garden 56230, queue row 1753. The exact target concerns every finite simple graph with at least one edge and no induced odd cycle of length at least five: partition its vertices so both induced clique numbers decrease, equivalently make every maximum-cardinality clique bichromatic. Edgeless induced graphs are exempt. Hereditary 2-divisibility is distinct from perfect divisibility; the five-cycle separates the notions.

The complete structural proofs establish color grouping, minimal-obstruction bounds and reductions, clique-precolor extension, exact clique-separator boundary compatibility and numerical consequences. At clique number k, the proved necessary conditions include order at least 3k−2, chromatic number at least 2k−1, minimum degree at least 2k−2, module-freeness, connected complement and a 2-connected maximum-clique edge core. A two-vertex clique separator at k=4 forces at least eighteen vertices. These conditions do not establish general clique-cutset exclusion.

The complete hypergraph proofs establish shadow realizability, the Fano obstruction, a chordal graph family whose maximum-clique shadow contains an odd hole, the incidence-two Euler construction for edge sizes at least three, and the sufficient Hall representative condition. Nonuniform and repeated labelled edges are treated with multiplicity-aware incidence. The chordal family remains divisible and is not a counterexample to the target. The Hall condition is not necessary.

## Prior credit and source limits

The omega=2 case is elementary bipartiteness; omega=3 follows by color grouping from the Chudnovsky–Robertson–Seymour–Thomas four-color theorem. Its full external decomposition proof is not re-audited here. The unrestricted clique-number-at-least-four target and general clique-cutset exclusion remain unresolved. No novelty claim or exhaustive current-literature certification is made.

Hu–Xu–Zhuang, arXiv:2603.01967v2, directly overlaps the minimum-degree, full-clique-number cutset-piece, incompatible-trace and minimum-disagreement blocking conditions. Those are credited prior necessary conditions, with complete independent derivations retained. Their distinct MNPD theorem is not substituted for an MN2D theorem. The separately qualified later Chen MNPD manuscript is discussed conditionally, and its finite computation was not replayed. Its examples retain induced five-cycles and do not settle this odd-hole-free target.

The complete source ledger and prior-credit audit distinguish theorem inspection, abstract-only inspection, retrieval failures, public preprint status and unaudited external full proofs. ### Accepted all-size results and exact limits

- If q=χ(H)>r=ω(H), then n≥2q−r+1, with equality exactly when the whole graph is K_(r−2)∨C5. If q≥r+2 or H has no induced C5, then n≥2q−r+2. Neither connectedness nor criticality is required.
- Every indivisible graph at clique number k≥3 has n≥3k. Every clique-cutset side of an induced-minimal indivisible graph also has at least 3k vertices. With separator size s and t sides, n≥s+t(3k−s). An edge separator has exactly two opposite forcing sides and requires n≥6k−2. At k=4, the edge and arbitrary-clique separator barriers are 22 and 20. These are necessary conditions, without an existence or sharpness assertion, and they do not establish unrestricted clique-cutset exclusion.

- For a finite simple graph with k=ω(G)≥3, let X consist of vertices belonging to at least three distinct maximum cliques of G. Incidences are counted in G, not recomputed in G[X]. Any prescribed coloring on P containing X extends if neither color contains a (k−1)-clique. Indivisibility forces X to be noncomplete, ω(G[X])≥k−1, χ(G[X])≥2k−3 and |X|≥2k−2. Under induced minimality, ω(G[X])=k: X contains a maximum clique, which does not mean X is itself a clique. These are necessary conditions, not a sufficient characterization.

The complete authored proofs and substantive independent audits are retained. The elementary boundary/core arguments do not depend on the external K4-free theorem.
