### Accepted results and limits

For a finite simple graph with clique number k≥3, let M be its distinct original maximum-cardinality cliques and let X contain the vertices occurring in at least three members of M. For a prescribed set P containing X, a prescribed coloring extends exactly when exhaustive singleton propagation terminates without conflict. Failure is equivalent to a matching signed P-tree. A failure certificate has at most |V minus P|+1 clique nodes and at most |M| nodes. The same propagation and tree arguments hold for distinct original sets of size at least three with outside-P incidence at most two; they do not require odd-hole-freeness. Repeated residual constraints are permitted. Incidence is counted in the original family, not recomputed in the induced core.

The complete accepted complexity correction explicitly supersedes the original proof and audit's false exponential representation-size assertion and qualifies the historical no-correction verdict. A defined P-tree is exactly an entire unmarked tree component of the dual multigraph. Consequently the exact extension formula has at most 2|M| signed clauses and at most 2L literal occurrences, where L is the total original incidence count. It can be constructed in O(n+L) time and space from integer-indexed incidence lists. Parallel edges exclude treehood; same-side boundary repetitions are deduplicated; overlap across the two sides makes either signed match impossible. This changes the representation-size assessment only. It does not establish polynomial-time maximum-clique enumeration, polynomial-time satisfiability, or the unrestricted conjecture. The O(2^|X|(n+L)) decision bound assumes the explicit original maximum-clique family is supplied.

For every k≥3, a connected chordal graph on 4k+1 vertices has exact original high-incidence core K_k disjoint K_(k−1), and exactly two valid core divisions fail to extend. Every whole graph in the family is divisible. This refutes arbitrary prescribed-core extension; it does not refute the existence of an extendible core coloring or the target conjecture. No size-minimality claim is made.

For an odd-hole-free indivisible graph with k≥4, the necessary bound is |X|≥3k−4, strengthened to |X|≥3k−3 if the core clique number is k−1. At k=4, X has at least eight vertices and contains a K4 without an induced-minimality hypothesis. The latter consequence uses the source-checked external Chudnovsky–Robertson–Seymour–Thomas four-color theorem; its full proof is not re-audited. These are necessary conditions, not existence or sharpness assertions. Original maximum cliques are distinguished from inclusionwise maximal cliques, and maximum-clique division is distinguished from perfect divisibility. The target assumes at least one edge. General odd-hole-free division and unrestricted clique-cutset closure remain unresolved. No novelty, human peer review, journal acceptance or full-solution claim is made.

### Exact projection and explicit correction

The exact projection uses distinct original maximum-cardinality cliques, never inclusionwise maximal cliques or incidences recomputed in the core. The prescribed set P contains every original vertex of maximum-clique incidence at least three. A selected obstruction tree is one whole unmarked component of the original low-incidence dual multigraph. Incidence-one marks exclude the whole component; retained parallel edges prevent treehood. Overlap of the two boundary unions discards the component, while repetitions on one side are deduplicated. The distinct-set extension requires all original sets to have size at least three.

For m original maximum cliques and L original incidences, the signed projection has at most 2m clauses and at most 2L literal occurrences. It is constructed in O(n+L) time and space from the supplied original incidence list. Both the complete authored correction and complete accepted complexity correction are included. They openly supersede the earlier false exponential-size assertion and qualify the historical audit's no-correction assessment. The earlier propagation, obstruction equivalence, certificate extraction and extension statements retain their exact scopes. Linear representation size is not an unrestricted satisfiability theorem and does not make maximum-clique enumeration from graph input polynomial.

Every nonempty tree of maximum degree at most k has the stated connected chordal realization with exact original maximum cliques, original core and unique effective obstruction component. These whole graphs are divisible. For trees with at least two nodes, the two bad core prescriptions are not divisions of the induced core. Arbitrarily large tree obstructions therefore do not give indivisible chordal graphs.

### Repeated leaves and the eight-core boundary

The separate repeated-leaf construction applies for k>=4. Its actual graph includes two diamond diagonals lying in no maximum clique. Simplicial reductions prove odd-hole-freeness at every rank without assuming that a maximum-clique shadow inherits odd-hole-freeness. Exactly two prescribed core colorings fail to extend, each with exactly one monochromatic (k-1)-clique; every other core assignment extends. These bad prescriptions are not core divisions, and each whole graph is divisible. At k=4 the example has 58 graph vertices, twenty maximum K4s and nine core vertices. It does not settle or exclude the eight-core frontier.

The original control history is explicit: deleting one diamond diagonal still left a valid odd-hole-free obstruction. The final historical checker therefore tested exact intended-diamond identity and rejected both single- and double-diagonal deletion. This was a control refinement; the intended construction and proof were unchanged.

### Structural bounds, minimality and prior credit

For k>=5, an odd-hole-free indivisible graph has at least 3k-3 original high-incidence core vertices, or at least 3k-2 if the core clique number is k-1. The stated critical-join equality forms are necessary conditions, not existence or sharpness claims. This initial draft records the accepted second-pass convex-reduction edition for problem 3326 / OPG-596, Linear Hypergraphs with Dimension 3. It preserves the ten accepted public files unchanged. The intended target is a finite covered loopless linear hypergraph whose vertex-edge incidence poset has order dimension at most three. Equivalently, use the finite covered Sperner linear convention, treating isolated singleton components separately. The indexed geometric objects are nonempty closed filled planar sets, and hyperedges are exactly the inclusion-maximal subfamilies with a common point. Pairwise intersection graphs, selected witnesses, disjoint interiors and contact-only representations are not substituted for this full-nerve requirement.

## Complete preserved deductions and exact limits

- Witness compression preserves the entire finite convex nerve: choose one common witness per maximal edge and take each vertex's hull of its incident witnesses. A maximum vertex degree of three yields points, segments or triangles. The degree counts incident hyperedges, not hyperedge size.

The exact target is an ordinary finite graph that fails to embed in N_(h+1), although every proper minor embeds in N_h, for some h>=1. The complete authored proofs and mathematical audits retain the genus-convention distinctions, all-proper-minor qualification, hopper and orientably-simple reductions, conditional doubling, triangle exclusion, minimum-degree and density arguments.

For h=2, the accepted necessary conditions are 3-connectedness, quarticity, triangle-freeness, K_(2,3)-freeness, at least twelve vertices, and two or three squares per edge, with at least one three-square edge. ### Second investigation: square selection, contraction rotations, and co-Heawood

The complete [second-edition proofs and certificates](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/research/3327-surface-reductions-20261012/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3327_square_rotation_frontier_20261012/README.md) and its full [independent edition acceptance](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/research/3327-surface-reductions-20261012/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3327_square_rotation_frontier_20261012/INDEPENDENT_EDITION_ACCEPTANCE.md) establish bounded partial results:

Equality E=nu excludes the orientably simple route for this graph. No edge-transitivity or all-minor claim is used.

The total residual cycle length outside the four-cycles is a positive multiple of four and is at least eight. Divisibility concerns the total, not each individual cycle length. These residual cycles are not eliminated.
- Complete rooted labeled generation through order 15 yields 3,354 leaves and 37 square-rich survivors: 31 explicitly checked square-disk surfaces of Euler genus two and six bipartite exclusions. ## Summary

Record two newly confirmed substantive investigations of problem 5500059 / AMR-054-0059 / TOPP 59, Most Circular Partition of a Square. The lifetime attempt count is unknown; this accounting does not assert that earlier attempts were absent, reset the budget, or certify any remaining attempt allowance. The general target remains unsolved.

The complete rational 100-cell square partition has maximum circumradius/inradius ratio strictly below 648023/500000 = 1.296046. It improves the separately preserved first edition's 92-cell bound 1.298322 and the identified source-reported bound 1.29950. These are comparisons of specific feasible bounds, without an exhaustive-literature priority claim.

For the infimum over finite polygonal partitions, the combined results give

G <= Gamma_fin < 1.296046,

where G = 1.288684461870457901325875... is the first edition's proved balancing constant. Every partition with at most N cells has worst ratio strictly greater than G + 1/(192 * 25^(N+2)). This very small N-dependent correction tends to zero and does not imply Gamma_fin > G.

The first edition also preserves the finite lower-bound proof, fixed-complexity existence proof, and a separately scoped non-tangent two-cell local certificate. The local patch is not a square partition and does not refute a conjecture restricted to tangent neighboring indisks.

The second edition also proves exact corner attachment and finite four-corner side patches approaching G, while explicitly leaving four side gaps and the interior uncovered. A direct single bridge between the specified constant-angle reflected separators has ratio at least 1 + 1/(4*t0^2) > 1.36. This is a restricted one-cell bridge obstruction: changing angles or using multiple bridge cells is not excluded, and no near-G complete-square construction follows.

## Final append: third, fourth and fifth investigations

### Current complete-square result

The third edition gives a complete 121-cell rational square partition with maximum circularity strictly below 1.295864. The fourth edition improves that complete-square witness to

G <= Gamma_fin < 1.295516,

with G = 1.288684461870457901325875... . The upper endpoint is exactly 1295516/1000000 and is strict. ### Boundary and interior-completion distinctions

The third edition proves finite boundary covers approaching G by unequal-angle transitions and gives an exact 56-cell boundary cover below 1.28878. It is not a full-square partition. The fourth edition proves that any completion retaining that original high-sided boundary patch, with ceiling below sqrt(2), needs at least 6,826 further interior pentagons and at least 6,882 total cells. Retaining all 136 cells requires at least 310 further pentagons and at least 446 cells in any completion below sqrt(2). At ceiling at most 13/10, the exact deficit identity is P5 = 310 + sum_{k>=7}(k-6)Pk + T + 2V4. Neither the 446-cell count nor any near-G finite completion is shown attainable.

The fifth edition also proves the sharp threshold R/r >= 1.290772978969... for arbitrary convex pentagons having two adjacent right angles, with an attaining tangential cyclic pentagon and independently positioned disk centers allowed. Its separate perturbation obstruction applies only to pentagonal caps on two specified full facets with exact equal-unfilled-sector-bisector seams. Other seam directions, facet subdivisions, hexagons and general completions remain outside that obstruction. A separately specified three-cell dead-end collar has an exact residual-angle obstruction at ceiling 13/10. That rejected configuration is distinct from the accepted 136-cell collar and proves no impossibility of completing the latter.

The general optimum remains unresolved. Unrestricted finite attainment, arbitrary infinite-partition equivalence, and finite completion of the near-G boundary/collar constructions remain unproved.

## Claim and exact scope

Publish one two-edition record for row 1759 / 8800049 / AMR-087-0049. Input is an explicitly represented finite field and a promised realizable ordinary, absolutely simple degree-six Weil polynomial. The theorem decides whether its abelian-threefold isogeny class contains a genus-three Jacobian over the original finite field in every characteristic, including two and three. It covers noninvertible Deligne ideals and every principal-polarization orbit. A successful test of one arbitrary polarization or a Jacobian only over an extension would not suffice.

2Q² + 18Q^(3/2) + 2321Q + 24√Q + 2270.
